parts.text: It’s the build-up in northern Australia – the time of year when heat and humidity get worse ahead of the wet season. Common

such as “going troppo” or “mango madness” give a sense of the effects. Tempers fray and tensions rise.

There’s now emerging evidence that humidity makes heat more dangerous. Humid

– where high temperatures combine with high humidity – are potentially more dangerous than dry heatwaves.

Elsewhere in the world, humid heatwaves are already claiming lives. Over 1,300 pilgrims died in Saudi Arabia in 2024 due to

levels of humidity and heat, while India and Pakistan have also been hard hit.

Our recent research in the Northern Territory found more people came to emergency departments during

humid heatwaves than comparable dry heatwaves.

The problem is, we’re not warning people about this combined threat. Australia’s heatwave warning systems focus only on temperature – not on humidity.

Why humidity matters

Intense heat

the body. Humidity can make this worse.

The human body relies heavily on sweating to regulate temperature. When sweat evaporates from the skin, it removes heat and helps keep the body cool. When humidity is high,

doesn’t work as well and it’s harder for the body to release heat and stay cool.

Humid conditions can boost the risk of heat-related illnesses such as heatstroke,

existing heart and lung conditions and put more strain on the bodies of people with chronic diseases.

High humidity can also contribute to poor sleep, reducing the body’s ability to recover during

hot periods.

Hot and wet conditions also provide optimal conditions for mosquitoes, ticks and parasites, which are vectors for the spread of key tropical diseases. Mould, bacteria and

are more likely to grow in high humidity, increasing the risk of lung and skin disease.

What we found in the Northern Territory

The top third of the Northern Territory has a monsoonal coastal climate prone to humidity, while the two thirds
is arid. This means we can analyse and compare humid and dry heatwaves across these environments.

reading.title: 主旨、理解与信息定位
reading.instruction: 阅读原文后回答 5 道选择题：1 道主旨、1 道内容理解、1 道段落细节、2 道信息定位。段落细节题以题干指定段落为准。

questions.prompt: Which statement best summarises the overall focus of this article?
options: Humidity increases the danger of heatwaves and deserves greater attention in public warnings.
Both artificial and natural wetlands can provide important habitat for young turtles.
Comparing Scotland and Wales reveals policy choices that influence recycling performance.
Wildfire damage is likely to increase, but affordable protective measures can reduce future losses.
questions.explanation: 把标题与全文各段的中心内容连起来判断主旨，避免把同一主题下的其他话题当成本文重点。
questions.evidence: Humid heatwaves – where high temperatures combine with high humidity – are potentially more dangerous than dry heatwaves.

questions.prompt: What did the Northern Territory research find about humid heatwaves?
options: They were associated with more emergency-department visits than comparable dry heatwaves.
They always caused fewer visits than every dry-weather event.
They were harmless whenever the temperature was high.
They eliminated the need for emergency care.
questions.explanation: 第 4 段提供了作答依据。正确选项用不同说法表达了文中的信息；请比较范围、数量、因果关系与限定词。
questions.evidence: Our recent research in the Northern Territory found more people came to emergency departments during intense humid heatwaves than comparable dry heatwaves.

questions.prompt: Which of the following statements is explicitly made in paragraph 13?
options: While more people sought emergency treatment during both dry and humid heatwaves, humid heatwaves were worse.
In many parts of northern Australia, heatwaves are projected to become more frequent and intense due to global warming.
The top third of the Northern Territory has a monsoonal coastal climate prone to humidity, while the two thirds inland is arid.
Hot and wet conditions also provide optimal conditions for mosquitoes, ticks and parasites, which are vectors for the spread of key tropical diseases.

questions.evidence: The top third of the Northern Territory has a monsoonal coastal climate prone to humidity, while the two thirds inland is arid.
